title: GenBreak: Red Teaming Text-to-Image Generators Using Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measures the ability of a red-teaming framework (using Large Language Models) to bypass safety filters in Text-to-Image (T2I) models and generate toxic content. As a subset of evaluating the 'hate' category, the paper measures the generation of hateful religious stereotypes, specifically targeting Jewish and Muslim groups (e.g., antisemitic and Islamophobic imagery).
findings: The study found that the GenBreak framework successfully generated adversarial prompts that bypassed safety filters to produce highly toxic and hateful images. Among its successful red-teaming attacks in the 'hate' category, the framework explicitly generated prompts resulting in antisemitic caricatures and Islamophobic content, demonstrating the vulnerability of both open-source and commercial T2I models to targeted religious hate generation.
